answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate the strongest-looking option first: memory_b1's rollback pattern is unavailable because compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so the fact that rollback worked on day 18 is irrelevant here. memory_b2 (regional failover) is the seductive match, since the degradation is confined to the primary region and the March case recovered in minutes. But the March record says nothing about write volume, and failover at settlement peak with heavy in-flight writes risks exactly the failure the primary objective forbids: losing customer writes to replication lag or a split cutover. A summary that records 'latency recovered' does not establish write durability, so I decline to lean on it at peak. add_capacity (memory_b3) was pre-provisioned ahead of a known peak; provisioning mid-incident will not land inside the 90-minute window. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained a failing downstream partner dependency; here the write path itself is degrading, so failing fast would shed the very writes I am trying to preserve. That leaves route_read_replicas: it is the only candidate that reduces load on the degraded primary without a cutover, is reversible, and cannot drop writes. I spend my single verification on memory_b5 rather than memory_b2, because b5 is the memory I am actually acting on and I need to know whether the day-55 recovery was genuinely caused by read-offload relieving write contention, or whether reporting load simply happened to subside; the summary asserts same-day recovery but no mechanism and no base rate. Note the shape of this inherited record: every entry is a success with no failure counts and no conditions of applicability, which is what an outcome-only archive looks like and is a reason to discount its apparent unanimity rather than treat it as six independent confirmations. I therefore stage read routing as a small guarded change with write-path p99 and replica lag as tripwires, and hold regional failover as the next-window action if offload does not bend the curve and the write peak has passed. I am not confident read contention is the true cause, given the timing correlation with the release two hours ago, which I cannot act on.
